utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we start, I would like to inform the parties that there is a problem with the new installed version of LiveNote. Version 8 seems to create some problems. I don't know what problems yet. The only way of solving it would have been to reinstall Version 7. Version 8 is now installed. That would have taken two hours and the Chamber has decided that it should be done somewhere today or tomorrow, but not at this very moment. Apart from that, may I ask the Prosecution, what time was Mr. Higgs scheduled to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. President. There is -- I am not aware of a specific time. There is a task that he was anxious to do in the UK, that is as much as I know. So my thinking was, if he finished here relatively early, then he still had a possibility of getting a flight back to London and doing whatever that task is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, would that mean, since Mr. Piletta-Zanin is not there, that if he would be here at 1.00 -- I still have to ask the Madam Registrar how much time is still available for cross-examination. It is my recollection that it was a bit more than one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not quite sure about that. So that would mean that, Ms. Pilipovic, I would say that if you would conclude the cross-examination not later than 12.00 then if Mr. Piletta-Zanin would arrive at 10.00 as indicated, then you would have until 12.00, you would have one hour and a half. I think that should do. If that is not enough, it is up to you to indicate that you would like to start already with the continuation of the cross-examination. Then I take it that the Prosecution is ready to call Mr. Gavrankapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, if it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours, we have had the weekend to peruse the forward copy of the decision of the Court pursuant to 92 bis. And subject to clarification from the Court, we would respectfully proceed or seek leave to proceed by calling Dr. Gavrankapetanovic as a viva voce witness and not pursuant to 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you are not allowed to call the witness under 92 bis, that doesn't necessarily mean that you are not allowed to call him as a viva voce witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And he would be taken by Mr. Manoj Sachdeva. May it please you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you are Mr. Gavrankapetanovic. Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration of which the text will now be handed out to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Gavrankapetanovic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to inform you at the beginning of your testimony, that it is possible that it will be interrupted since there is still one hour, one hour and a half left for another witness, and he has to leave this afternoon. So it might be that in the course of your examination, it will be interrupted and we will then resume later. And that will, as far as I can see, later today then. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good morning Witness. I am wary of my pronunciation so can you state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. My name is Faris Gavrankapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you remain in Sarajevo during the period 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And are you presently employed?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is your occupation please?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I am a doctor. I am a specialist in general surgery. Currently I am a general manager of the university in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "the university in Sarajevo" is that the name of a hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It has a different name which is not an official name. It is the clinical centre of the University of Sarajevo, known as the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And as general manager, can you briefly explain to the Court the responsibilities that go with that position.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well it is a managerial position. I am managing the staff of the hospital, employed at the hospital. I am a manager organising the work and I am also organising the payment of salaries for employees paid out through the funds for the costs of the hospital and also I am responsible for everything that goes on in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You say that you are responsible for everything that goes on in the hospital. Can you be a little bit more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am responsible for everything that is to do with my post. It is the government of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina which is responsible for the hospital and the four cantons. So that is the government of the Federation, the Sarajevo canton as the main founder, together then Sana and Una --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could you slow down the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, may I ask you to talk a bit slower because the interpreters cannot follow your speed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can perhaps look at the cursor on your screen. As soon as it stops then, at least they have translated everything. I wouldn't say that you also have to stop until it stops moving, but please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do your responsibilities include anything in respect to the record keeping at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they do. But if you just allow me, I would like to come back to finish the parts that I started. The managing rights are held by the government of the Federation and the four cantons that I mentioned, the Sana-Una canton, the Central Bosnia canton, the Karejovo de Doboj canton, the Sarajevo canton and they represent the managing board which executive director and then the director is responsible for the executive function. That means that I am responsible also for the documentation, that is for the records that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. So going back to my question with respect to the records, what exactly is your role?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't keep records myself personally. At the post that I occupy, I don't keep the records. But I am responsible for the records that is kept by others. If this is to do with entries, parameters of entries for protocols these are kept by the people who have secondary school we call them medical technicians and nurses regardless of whether they are women or men. They are the ones that keep the records. A doctor enters a diagnosis, a prognosis, and also what has been done, that is the treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to show you some records in a moment, but I would just like you to tell us, were you director-general of Kosevo hospital during the conflict, that is 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I was a doctor, a surgeon working in traumatology. I worked in the hospital as I have explained before which is the treatment of the injured. Before me, there were two general managers, their names are mentioned in the statement that I gave to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I am a general manager I was elected on the 7th of November 2000, and considering that this is a very large institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: For a whole month, there was an appeals procedure and I started to work on the 19th of December 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, I would like to show the witness some documents. Unfortunately they are contained within the 92 bis package with the witness, so they are not individually numbered. But I think the best course of action would be to go through the ERN that are indicated on the records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, how many approximately would you like to show to the witness. Are we talking about three or ten or?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Probably four documents in total, but three batches containing a number of pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, for practical reasons we will start with the bundles, since Madam Registrar would not be able to separate each individual document. But I take it all those that are working with it, perhaps the Defence, the Bench and the Prosecution, perhaps at a later stage could separate them, but let's start with the bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: As you wish, Mr. President. While those documents are being handed to you witness, if you were to see records from Kosevo Hospital would you be able to recognise them?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, would you be able to guide the usher in that way that only the documents you intend to show to the witness will be in front of him and then we will find our way through the...

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you can just take some time to peruse those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate to us what is in front of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a batch of -- a document containing roughly 12 pages. The ERN goes from 02156586 to 02156602. And there is also an English translation which is 03014354, although I don't believe you have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, are these papers in numerical order?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, they are. There should be numbers at the bottom of the page. I think with this particular document the best course of action is to go by the ERN numbers which are at the top right-hand corner of the document and there are two numbers that we are talking about. The number 02156586 which is the larger print.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, I think we found them. On the other hand I have a document in my hands which is the same number as well, which is a totally different document. May I just ask the usher to show this document to you and see whether it also starts with 02156586. It is difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know. But has it the same number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Not the same number. The number on the protocol is 02156586. I think it is actually the name number. But I suspect that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that we are talking about documents like this and would you please take care not to put the same ERN numbers on different documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I am guided Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Doctor, have you had a chance to peruse these documents?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on these documents?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what this document depicts, or what is this document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you allow me, I noticed here several dates of injured people, of injured patients, who are admitted to the emergencies, to the emergency centre. And the abbreviation is "CUM" and the dates are 4th of February, 5th of February, both 1994. And then I saw the 22nd of January, of the 23rd of January 1994, 12th of July. I would say this is 1993. Then 13th and 14th of July 1993. 30th and 31st of May and the 1st of June 1993. I think there are in all 17 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. We will get back to the details later. Can you just say, do these documents emanate from your institution, that is, the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what type of document is this?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: These are admissions details for the main protocol which is kept and located at the emergency centre where -- as of 1993 to date, every injured person or sick person goes through there, is admitted there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this represent the first record contact for a patient that comes to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we can now -- if you can now look at the first page. If you see on the top right-hand corner, a number 02156586, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And on the extreme left, you will see the first column. If you could tell us what that column depicts please.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a number of the injured, the serial number, probably from the start of the year, from the 1st of January 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Next to that column, there is a column headed "Datum."

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see the date underneath that, the first date underneath that title?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. 4th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you look at the number 694 and go down and come to number 701 on the same page, do you see the date next to that number?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. 5th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If you now go through the pages until you arrive at the number eight, the number on the left hand column, 802. The ERN page is 02156595 on the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see the date 5/2/1994, there?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what these entries are? In other words, from number 694 on the 4th of February 1994 to number 802?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are injured people but 694 was the day before, the number given the day before on the 4th of February 1994, and the next date begins with 701 on a page 02156586, that is 5th of February 1994. All of these people injured from number 701 until number 802 were taken care of. They went through the emergency centre without -- regardless whether these people were taken care of and injured or those who were brought already dead or those who died during treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So everybody that came to the hospital, that on the 4th and 5th of February was recorded down on this protocol. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Everybody who was admitted to Kosevo Hospital, yes. Since there was another hospital, there were two other hospitals, Kosevo was the biggest and there were two more hospitals, one in the centre of town, general hospital, and another one in the Dobrinja area, that was the general hospital as well, treating patients from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can now go to page 2, the second page of that batch, please. If you go to the sixth column from the left, you will see the words, [B/C/S spoken]. Do you see that column there?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I mean just a second. It should be 02156587.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Correct. Do you see the time depicted on that page?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the serial number 711?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, 711 is included on that page. But if you look at the column where the time is depicted, do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Hour, 12.35.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the court why the time is recorded down this page and the next page as 12.35 for each admitted patient?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, first of all, generally speaking, we always enter the time of admission, especially in 1992, 1995, both before and after that. Whenever we talk about car accidents, any incidents of violence or anything like that because it is particularly important from the point of view of forensic medicine, because you have to be able to tell the exact time when the patient was admitted to hospital. So we always take care to specify that. In this case, there was a huge number of patients brought to the hospital at the same time. Quite a few of them. I think we can tell exactly how many if we go through these papers. And they were all brought to the hospital at approximately the same time, so we recorded this hour for the simple reason, so as to separate the records for these patients from others who were brought to the hospital from other places, but there were less of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why did you want to separate the records for these patients? Where were they brought from?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can tell, it is to 12.35, the 5th of February 1994, it is the time when the dead and wounded were brought to the hospital and the cause was the event at the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say, "event at Markale" can you be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately, there were quite of few events, but the one that we are discussing at the moment took place on a Saturday, the 5th of February. As far as I can remember, the period before that event was rather calm and tranquil and I suppose quite a few people went to the market. And then a shell landed and injured quite a few people, more than 100, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please now go to page 02156598. It is the 5th to the last page. Do you see the record number there 12/27? It is the third row down.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see the date next to that column?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do; the 12th of July 1993. The 12th of July, according to this register.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you now continue to page, the second last page 02156601. Do you see the record number 995 on the right hand -- left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: 995 I don't. There is a 925, if this is the page you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes. And what is the date in the column next to it?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 1st of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally on this document, if you can move back to page 02156597. Do you see the number 433 on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the date 21st -- 22nd, 1, 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That document can be removed. Mr. President, perhaps this document can be marked with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: This would be 3737A. And also if I may have a translation of this document, which is 3737.1 -- A.1. With your leave, Mr. President I have another document to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May we have a copy of the translation, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these ERN numbers 03014353 up until 03014400, is that the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. Mr. President I've handed the witness document -- if I should give you the reference number. It is 02156603 to 02156612.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pronounce figures slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva it would certainly have assisted us if the copies were made such that we could see ERN numbers on it. I see the first one and I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the ERN numbers are on every other page. Essentially, one is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it. I see it now, yes. So every two pages bear one ERN number. Is that front and back of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: It is the front of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But Mr. Sachdeva, there is no ERN numbers on the back of the page or the right-hand side of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Correct, it is the same page, but it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you please repeat the last page. Would that be last three digits 612?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Doctor, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This document is the patients' register for patients admitted to the operation theatre or the operation theatres, because there is more than one. And they are at the emergency department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So I take it this is a separate protocol for a different department in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the register listing the patients for whom it was decided that they had to be operated on. So, in other words, they were taken from the emergencies to the operating theatre, to the part of the hospital where the operating theatres are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you turn to the second page please.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the beginning of that page? I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you look at the left-hand side, it has the record number 344 on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see a date next to that?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes I do; the 4th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And then further down that page do you see the 5th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. 341.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sir, this document depicts people who were brought on the 4th and 5th of February and required surgery. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there is an error. It is not 341, but 351. [In English] 351. [Interpretation] Are you talking about the -- could you repeat the question please. Yes, the first one is 351, the 5th of February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. So this document shows record of people who were admitted for surgery on the 4th and 5th of February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If you can now go to the page reference 02156607. 02156607. Do you have that there?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't. I don't have the top of the page. I suppose it is the one I am looking at at the moment, but the top bit is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see halfway down that page the number 227, the record number, pertaining to a "Du sa hamdo" [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not the one I am looking at. No, I found it now, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see 227 now, the record number, and the date next to that?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The 22nd of January 1994. The date is not clear but since the dates directly before and after are the same, it must be the 22nd of January 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if you go to the right-hand side and third column from the right which says "Naca tesir" [phoen]. What does that mean, please?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: "Naca tesir" refers to the anesthesiologist. Whenever there is surgery, and the protocols refer to the diagnosis, the type of surgery, the anesthesia, and then the list of people participating.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of these people recorded here?

utterances.speaker: FARIS GAVRANKAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: All doctors, yes, I do. As to the technical staff, perhaps not every single one of them, but most of them yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. I would like to show you one more document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, you gave numbers to the other documents. Are you doing the same here and are you providing translations, or?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President. This document can be marked 3737B. And the translation is ERN 03034087.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By pronouncing the numbers, would you please slow down, because that is even more difficult than any other thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will repeat, 03034087. 3203034110.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that that would be P3737B.1?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Mr. President, perhaps we can have a break and the examination-in-chief so as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if this would be a moment where you could stop before going to your next document. Then the Defence could continue to cross-examine Dr. Higgs, and then for certain, they will conclude by 12.00, since you have got one hour and a half hours left as far as my accounting goes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: This would be a good moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gavrankapetanovic, as I indicated before, there might be an interruption in your examination. This is the moment where we have to switch to another witness. I apologise for that, but practical reasons more or less forced us to proceed this way. May I instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony in this court. Yes. Mr. Usher, would you then please escort Mr. Gavrankapetanovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you perhaps at the same time bring Mr. Higgs in once -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Higgs. Please be seated. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. The Defence will now resume its cross-examination. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I would like to come back to our last issue that we spoke about. You will remember that we spoke about this area and I would like us to have back on the ELMO the same document which was a map in relation to the incident number five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be P3727. 5th page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could zoom on the area that we are most interested in, which is above number five. Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, to come back to what we spoke of earlier when you were here last, you told us that you were able to see the routes in the southern part, south of the green line, which is what we call here, the Seven Woods Sedam Suma. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir, could you please confirm to the Chamber if this is the case, that a mortar, would it be of 120 millimetre, is that a much simpler weapon to transport and to install than it would be the case for another type of artillery weapon?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 120 millimetre mortar would be easier to assemble than an artillery piece, but more difficult than a medium mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you for your answer. Sir is it true that it is perfectly feasible to fire such a mortar from numerous locations, though bearing in mind that if we are on a sloping terrain, that it is equally possible, thanks to the work of the engineers to make a small horizontal base where a mortar could be placed; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible to fire a mortar from any location like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir therefore, and being objective as an expert it is true that you cannot formally rule out the possibility that a firing would come from the lower part of this line, that is, from the area south from the line?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible from the evidence that I have seen to discount this 100 per cent. But what you must take in mind is the view of the low area from the high areas to the north, and positioning a mortar in view of an enemy or opposing forces who are able to look down on that position, would not be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I thought so. But I would like you to answer by a yes or no, if that is possible, to the question that I have asked. Could you categorically rule out the firing from this area yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is difficult to answer this question in just a "yes or no," because with my military expertise, it would be extremely unlikely to place a mortar in this location but also I could not 100 per cent say they did or they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is that you could not exclude that. The question was quite clearly about whether you could, I would say, position, even if it was for a very short time a mortar there, and whether it would be wise to do so, and whether it would be effective to do so, if you want to look at a specific target. That is a different question, but the answer is so clearly, no, you cannot exclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday on a photograph that you were shown, you identified three elements, and you were able to give the names, one out of three, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, could you please confirm if this is the case, since first of all you spoke about a reductor? There is a problem with the interpretation. I don't remember what was the term used. I believe that you were speaking of a ring of reduction. I am going to rephrase my question. What was the name of the three elements, the three pieces that you identified?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two pieces were the shape you would expect to see from the fuse adapter -

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I apologise. I am talking about the adapter. In relation to this adapter, is it true that in fact this is an adapter of diameter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the part that connects the fuse to the body of the round.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I will later on ask you to have a look at a piece. I don't know what the number is, because I didn't have time to see. But with the assistance of Madam Registrar, we will find out immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D167. This piece could be put on the ELMO please, with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please assist, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The question that I am going to ask you, sir, is the following: On the basis of the sketch that you see before you or the -- could you please identify the adapter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fuse adapter is located in the area just below the fuse, which will be on this picture in that area just there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir the expert is indicating on the top of the grenade on top of the fuse itself. Sir, on the two drawings --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it is a translation problem. But the answer in English or rather the description in English provided by my friend reads "the fuse adapter is located in the area just below the fuse which will be --" I am sorry. The expert is indicating on the top of the grenade on top of the fuse itself. Now, that description is at least open to much ambiguity because it doesn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase, Mr. President. But in French it was very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in French, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I was listening to the French channel. Please proceed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the top part of the body of the round, and in the part which is immediately below of the fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, could you please indicate where the fuse is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating the top part of the shell. We can see just below the fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please point again to the adapter.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to the top part of the body of the round below the fuse. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, might it also be noted that all of the references so far by the witness have been to the diagram indicated as LM 120 millimetre, to make clear it is not to the other two. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I had mentioned very clearly that this was showing the inside of the shell. There is only one on the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that the adapter is also used to allow the adaptation on the body of the round for a different type of a fuse. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Different types of bomb allow for different fuses to be fitted into that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, is it true, as far as you know, that for such shells, a fuse has an immediate effect -- no. With a fuse which works immediately, and the fuse which has a time delay don't have necessarily the same diameter or the same section?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Different fuses can be fitted to different rounds. Not all rounds can be fitted with a selection of fuses. Normally, the fuse would be what we call a "direct action fuse." This would detonate on impact. Most direct action fuses also have what we call a "delay setting," which delays the fuse from detonating by approximately point 05 of a second. That type of fuse is normally fitted as standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like to ask you to have a look at a second piece which would be piece D168 please. Mr. President, on this document, and there are some markings in Serbian, but we do not wish to submit them. What we are mostly interested in is the drawing which is on the top right part of this drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, does the drawing which can be seen on the top right part, could we please focus a little better. Thank you. Which is the top right side of this document, does this drawing correspond to the -- to what an adapter looks like? Although, it was presented as having exploded -- no a section.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the drawing, it is difficult to say, but it does look the type of shape you would expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, therefore, when we have an adapter, just to make things simpler, could we say that this is a fixing ring; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Fixing ring, yes, that is what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And could we say that in some cases, these rings are also adapters used as adapters, which would allow the bottom part to attach itself to the body of the shell, and then on the top, that they would be screwed into the fuse [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So, sir it is true that for one round, one shell, which was fired, there would only be one adapter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just for the better understanding, could you please look with me at page 25, lines 19 and 20. Is it correct that you said "and then on the top"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a little blinded, but I will try and see. That was page 25, line 19 and 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Bottom part would attach -- say and then on the top the fuse would be screwed in instead of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. It is the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask for line 20, 19 and 20, to correct that the fuse would then screwed in the adapter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Thank you very much. I will avail myself of this opportunity to ask for a technician, because I only have half of my screen today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, it is true that when a shell is fired, there is only one adapter for this shell; yes? You already said, but I would like you to --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to ask again for the photograph that we saw last Friday. It is this photograph which was shown to the witness and I believe we saw some 73 pieces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the one that is now in front of you I think with the small -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the piece on which the witness marked one, two, three.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, just to make things very clear could you please mention what are the two pieces of the adapter that you identified?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are numbers one and two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. If we can still keep this photograph, and then if the witness can be shown our exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is D61, it is an old exhibit, D61. I would like to see it before just to make sure that it is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am showing you this photograph because it seems much clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be put on the ELMO, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We agree that this is the same photograph, Witness? Do you recognise the same items?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, sir, we worked on the same photograph that you identified, and now, with the assistance of the usher, I would like to have distributed another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. President, I am looking at the clock and I believe the time is perfect for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you -- Mr. Usher, could you please return the two documents to the Registrar and we will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, before I give you the opportunity to resume your cross-examination, I would like to inform the parties that this morning, early, before we started, there was some discussions with the court management and using empty courtroom time on another case is not that easy, since that case was sitting in the morning usually as well. So we can't sit in two courtrooms in the morning. Until now, the result is that we might sit on Thursday for the full day. We still have to consider what kind of breaks we would use, but that would be from early in the morning, 9.00, up to 7.00 in the evening. So that would at least give us quite a number of hours extra. That, as it stands, at this moment. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to take this opportunity now to refer to something General Galic told me because this matter was raised last Friday. And he confided that he did not feel up to being here for such a long period of time. And he has assiduously attended all hearings so far, but a full day of hearings from his point of view is unbearable. Unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will hear at a later stage -- one day it is not for the whole week. But we will, at a later stage, not in the presence of the witness, we will hear the comments of General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to inform you that we will be calling a certain witness tomorrow who is the subject of discussion last Friday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do understand what you mean. Then, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. With the assistance of the usher, document 169 to be circulated. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me just remind you sir, about before the break I submitted to you a document which you identified as being the same and so we will continue on the copy of this last document. It has been renumbered now, 169, for the proceedings. Sir, these adapters, can you find them again on this image; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, we are now going to engage in the following exercise. We will point a compass on the arch of the circle defined by these two elements that is going to yield various circles, A, A 1, B, B 1, and then we can look at either a smaller or bigger section of what appears on the screen. Sir, does it appear that there are two different diameters for these adapters?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The adapter shape will give you these two diameters, because it is cone shaped and not symmetrical.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, quite. But when it comes to this screw, the internal screw, normally for the inside, it refers to a vertical section?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The inner-part circle of the adapter would be vertical, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it correct that the circles with -- outlined here are on the inside, the inner parts?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be difficult to tell from the pieces of shrapnel because they are not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. But you will agree with me that these circles were not placed on the outside, but on the inside of this curve?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, is it correct that what we see here are two quite different diameters. We see twice two different diameters. A, on the one hand and B on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could we then draw a probable conclusion that we are dealing with two different types of adapters here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shape of the adapter because it is always smaller at the top than it is at the base, will give you fragments both of one of a small diameter and one of a larger one. The inside features of this shrapnel do not have to come to meet the vertical of the smallest diameter because inside of these, there would normally be a thin metal chamber which then supports the fuse and it is that chamber that is vertical, not the body of the adapter which these two pieces appear to be from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please, usher, show us once again, the document 168.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to take advantage of that short break, at some stage might we have access to D61. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show 168 once again whilst leaving this on the screen. [In English] 169 -- 168, sorry. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, the orifice that we see on the inside of the adapter to the right which corresponds to the upper part of the body of the shell, doesn't it show on the inside a screw shape of a diameter which is always equal; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just confirm which part, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The scheme, the pattern that you have on the right-hand side which represents an adapter, can you see it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Isn't it true that on the inside it incorporates a screw shape fitting bit which must necessarily have a parallel and a vertical section?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The base of the adapter which would fit into the body of the round, which would be on your drawing, the base there, that screw thread, yes, would be vertical to screw into the body of the round. The inner part where the fuse would then screw into, again, yes, it would be vertical because of the liner that I have already spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we agree that the two threads of those screw, both on the inside and both on the outside are vertical?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So we can agree that if we find a hollow part of an adapter, in other words, the part corresponding to the gap or the void of an internal screw thread, it can only have one single diameter, is it true?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it not true that with reference to the two parts of the adapter that you yourself have pointed out, these pieces appear to have a different sizes of this gap or void on the inside? Does it appear so?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are a different internal side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, if you had these two pieces in front of you, would you be in a position to identify them better, more accurately?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, is it correct that the chemical and mechanographical analysis would allow to identify the quality of the metals used in order to manufacture such-and-such a bullet; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Expert, is it correct in theory that generally speaking for one round, one should come across one single type of diameter? What I mean is round fired, and in theory; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you confirm which diameter you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It doesn't matter which one. I am simply referring say to a 120 millimetre shell or an 82 millimetre shell or mortar. Once you find it once it had exploded, or even if you find it intact on that device, you can only find one single type of adapter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So if there is only one single adapter with one single internal diameter in order for the fuse to be fitted to it in principle you can't come across two different types of diameters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Expert, if -- well, let's assume we were to find two completely different types of diameters, wouldn't the conclusion then be -- and I am referring to the central screw thread on the inside and vertically speaking -- would the conclusion then be that at least two shells had been fired because we would have two different sizes of diameters? Would it be the logical conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To come to that conclusion, you would have to identify the internal screw threads. On this diagram, or this picture, you cannot identify the screw threads.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, unfortunately we don't have the devices here. I am just talking about the principle of the matter, about a theory. If one were able to demonstrate that two different types of diameters were found on the spot, would the experts conclusion be that there had been at least two types of shells? Because we have got two different sizes for the diameter. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned before, to ascertain that, you either need to definitely have the threads or to have the chamber which fits inside the adapter which is the vertical chamber. The outer parts of the adapter which these may be, you would not expect them to be the same diameter. The problem from the picture is that we can't see because we don't have the physical evidence that they are the internal dimensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. However, we don't have the devices, unfortunately. We asked for them but we don't have them. My question is the following: On a purely theoretical level, yes or no, that if we were to find, let's assume, two totally different diameter sizes corresponding to this inner screw thread, would it be true that it would necessarily point out to there being two different types of fuses or shells; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I am going to submit to you, a document 170. Perhaps we could place it properly on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me explain this to you. This is a photocopy of the part of the previous figure that we were interested in, but now we have carried out some very simple measurements there to ascertain the size, on the basis of what we had been able to define. Now is it correct sir, that the external size of the item marked by "A" is smaller than the item marked by "B"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Let me just mention for the sake of the transcript, that this is a photocopy of a part of the photocopy that we were looking at earlier on. I have no further photocopies, but I am now going to put to you a certain number of other technical questions. Could you just confirm that there is a difference in the rate of penetration of the bullets or the shells, depending on the terrain, that is whether they hit the macadam, the cement or the concrete or what have you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness what is the depth, not just of the crater, but of something which we occasionally call a tunnel, that you would expect to see within the framework of a soft terrain, on the one hand, and a hard terrain on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is difficult to answer precisely because all ground types give slightly different answers. But where you talk about "the tunnel" I presume you mean the fuse furrow. On soft ground, this can go down into the ground anything really soft ground ending up to half a metre. Hard ground, it could then be limited to no fuse furrow at all or a very short one of a matter of only of a few centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And on a hard ground the stabiliser which as a consequence would be at the very -- at the tail end of the shell, could also get burrowed into the ground; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can, but again it is affected by those points that I raised in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you expect on a hard ground such as ground covered by a layer of concrete, would you expect the stabiliser not just to break it up, but to penetrate in greater depth into the ground underneath?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the harder surfaces, the tail-fins tend not to dig in deep as on soft ground, but they still do. The amount by which they penetrate the ground, it is very difficult to be specific exactly how far they will go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You have mentioned, sir to have seen quite a few rounds being shelled. Have you often seen on hard ground tail-fins which were completely dug into the ground? When I talk about "hard ground" I mean about a surfacing which is not soil, but a layer of macadam or concrete?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question in its present composition. I would ask that the word "completely" be qualified. Does my learned friend mean that the tail-fin is completely, that is, wholly consumed within the earth or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I meant, completely. Full penetration, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And dug in very deeply.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen medium mortar rounds on tarmac where the tail-fins have been below the level of the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question was rather, whether it is an exception or the rule?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On very hard ground such as tarmac, it happens less than it would do on soft ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I take it then it would be an exception rather than the rule, on the basis of what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not an exception. It still happens, but a lot lower percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir would the rate of penetration be different depending on what sort of fuse you have got, a delay or a direct taction fuse or a delay setting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Just very briefly, in what way?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A delay setting allows the round to travel further approximately point 05 of a second before detonating. This gives the round time to big into the ground before it explodes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, is there a way of determining after an explosion whether it was direct action or a delay setting fuse?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The crater examination on a delay setting, the investigators should identify it immediately because it gives a completely different crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In what way is it a completely different crater?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the round is exploding further into the ground, the pattern given off by the shrapnel is a more contained inside the crater. So you don't get the normal mortar pattern.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have you seen, sir, any sort of a picture or reproduction of Markale crater?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, you have?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On the basis of your considerations and on the basis of your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. expertise do you believe that that could have been a direct action fuse that would have been used, had the shell never been fired to land on the market?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crater that is visible in the pictures seems to be that of a direct action fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thus, it is the type of crater whereby the shell is not likely to dig in very deeply into the ground. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would now like to move on to other matters, just very briefly. You spoke about types of explosion. Is it true, is it exact, yes or no, that the age of ammunition could be a factor that would be detrimental on the quality of the materiel that is to explode; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The top of ammunition will affect the explosive effectiveness of the round.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about their age, sir. And for the transcript, we are speaking of the same thing, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. The older the ammunition tends to be less effective than the newer types.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you said that it is less efficient. It is less efficient -- less effective on various levels? For instance, it's aerodynamic its flight capacity on the one hand and on the other hand, its explosive effectiveness, that is its ability to explode or not explode, whatever the case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, the older ammunitions have slightly shorter ranges and they tend to be less powerful on detonation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And in relation to the flight?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the older ammunitions, yes, can be less accurate than the newer types.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And very briefly sir, do you know what it means M-38, 1 or 2 or 3?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just those numbers on their own don't mean a great deal, but they appear to be batch numbers that you would sometimes get on certain ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know what this means, specifically?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am going to ask you the same thing for three series of numbers, M-52 R-1, M-64 R-1 R-2, and M-72 RR-123.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without obviously some reference it is impossible to say, but they appear to be model or batch numbers of weapons or ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Let's assume that these are batch numbers and that "R" correspond to the remount, have you ever seen any firing tables for R-1, R-2, R-3?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be specific on that. I have seen the firing tables that were contained in the report for this incident. I can't remember if that was specifically that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir if you have seen the tables, do you know exactly which tables you have seen in numbers yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The table I have seen is the one that is in the UNPROFOR report of this incident, whichever table that is, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Which incident? Which incident?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the 120 millimetre, it would be for incident five, the market incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, would you agree with me that for each of the shells, i.e., for each of the types, the models R-38 or M-52 there would be a firing table which relates to it, which corresponds to it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Is it true that these firing tables are different, they differ because the M72 has different qualities to the R-38 model; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they will differ.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, how were you able to see a firing table when we don't even know if allegedly the shell that had hit on the market is 38, 52, 64, or 72?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question is unfair. The witness has said that his recollection is that the firing table was attached to the UNPROFOR report. Given that answer, this question lacks any probative value, because really, it questions the appropriateness of the UNPROFOR investigators, including the firing table in the report. Mr. President, further, might I have access to that report it is PT -- I'm sorry, P2309A.1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to be able to follow the questioning, I think it would be good if we would have that report available. Is it not attached to the report of Mr. Higgs? That is what I am just asking myself. I think it is not. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, Mr. President. But that is not going to change anything to what the witness said, that there are different tables, according to different models. He was given a table, and since he doesn't know which one he saw, and we don't even know on the basis of which table the calculations had been done. So at this stage, I think that the response is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness has told us which tables he used. I haven't got clearly at my mind at this moment what is in these tables or not. But he also told us that he has no clear recollection exactly of the content of these tables. And you can't expect the witness to have all the figures in his head. So if the matter is dependent on the table and the content of the table, it would be fair if both the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question is not related to the contents of the tables but on the years of the tables, that is, is this a table which relates to model 38 or to the 52 or to the 64 or to 72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... knows that by heart, there is no problem, but if he does not, and part of the objection against the question was that we would not be able to check at this very moment the relevance of the question is without having had access to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you only received one table yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you do not know any more whether this table was relating to 38, 52, 64 or 72 model. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, who gave you this table?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. At page 40 line 16, I think it is in the English transcript, the witness clearly said that the table was part of the UNPROFOR report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That doesn't mean that he received the UNPROFOR report from the UNPROFOR. That is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: True, Mr. President. The question therefore should be in relation to the UNPROFOR report. In other words, who gave you the UNPROFOR report, rather than who gave you this table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the tables are in the UNPROFOR report, I did understand the question to be that in what way did you receive this UNPROFOR report containing the tables. But if I am not correct --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the objection overruled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may ask the witness how he received these tables in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who handed you the report and the tables which were attached to it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I started my investigation, I was given those reports by the UN -- the Prosecutor's part of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But you are certain there was just one table, one single table?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is just the one table in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. Sir could you be very quick and brief because the time is passing very quickly, also for the Prosecution. Could you confirm if this is the case, that it is practically impossible to see with the naked eye the trajectory of a shell?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible if you stand directly behind the mortar to see it leaving the barrel on its upward flight. But it is nearly impossible, I have never known anybody to see one passing overhead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it true that the mortar itself is static, a mortar is static and that it is not going to appear as ball of fire in the sky or something similar?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the mortar that is firing?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about the bomb, the projectile, I am talking about the shell.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously the mortar bomb cannot be static, it is moving. But it does not give any trail or noticeable signs as it passes through the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a mistake in term on my part, that is what I wanted to say. Therefore, the only possibility that one has of seeing it is to be either in the axis of the firing or on the back of the mortar, on the other side, on the back of the mortar?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, Mr. Expert, that bearing in mind the relative speed of sound, if we hear it, we hear a mortar shell for less time than the trajectory that this shell has achieved?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, by the time you hear the mortar firing, working on the speed of sound, the round would have already have left the barrel and is already some distance along its trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Quite. Now, to come back to the conditions of firing, is it correct, sir, that the conditions in certain locations could be very different, depending on the altitude, whether it is high ground or in the valley, these conditions could greatly affect the firing of a mortar shell? I am talking about theory, a principle.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it correct that if these conditions can change very quickly, firing that takes place on the -- that is fired on the basis of the same coordinates without modifications could have a quite considerable errors in firing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you fail to take them into account, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, a number of witnesses or experts spoken about what we would call a "safety zone" safety area of about 200 to 400 metres from the target. Could you confirm in theory this zone, this area of 200-400 metres?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you talk about safety zone in this point, are you relating to the effectiveness or lethal area of the round or the built in safety parameters by the firers and their own troops?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about the second hypothesis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, most armies will build in a safety zone to stop them shelling their own troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And sir this safety zone is established for two reasons. I believe the first being is the possibility of error, and the second being is obviously the lethal zone danger of firing on one's own troops. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So, in other words, all the armies that you know about use this margin to protect themselves, as soon as these such mistakes can take place. Is that how I should understand it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JAMES HIGGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
